chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:
Regarding dye (for hair/beard), there are three qualities: it inspires awe in battle, it increases love from women, and it increases sexual desire.
ai.seo_question: What are the three benefits of using hair dye according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the practical wisdom behind the Prophet's tradition of using henna or indigo, framing it not merely as grooming but as a means of enhancing masculine presence (*mehyabah*) in battle and increasing marital intimacy. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on balancing spiritual devotion with natural human desires, viewing physical attractiveness as a valid form of worship when done with the right intention.
